reviews.t: I don't know how you can beat it for the money....
reviews.x: I have been a faithful user of Braun Oral-B rechargeable toothbrushes for about 5 years.  This brush does a great job just like the brushes I've used in the past.  I like the 2 minute timer.  This feature is typically not available in their entry level brushes, but this one has it, and I found out quickly that I wasn't brushing for nearly long enough. (now I am)  The handle on mine does not even get warm when it is charging...and I have never seen this issue with a Braun Oral-B brush...doesn't s

I was a bit skeptical of this item because prices were all over the place for similar products. I tried this one (very reasonable price) and I am delighted. It works great, light weight, easy to use and holds the charge well. So far so good.

reviews.t: gray metal gets in your toothpaste
reviews.x: I bought this toothbrush in January and also one for my daughter. By early summer we both noticed a strange metallic taste and the toothpaste in our mouths was gray instead of white. Black drops started coming out of the handle and it became clear that metal from inside the handle was mixing with the toothpaste and getting into our mouths. Other than this problem I thought the device was great but this is just not acceptable so I am buying a different brand.

reviews.t: Great but needs better battery life
reviews.x: Its cheap and is great for cleaning behind those wisdom teeth. I wish the battery life was longer than 5 days though. Replacement heads are easy to find and cheap as well.
This brush is easy to  use, timer is very helpful.  i have had great reviews from my dental hygenist since I've been using the Oral B.  It's priced right too.

I wanted to shop around for an electric toothbrush because, despite my best efforts to brush at least twice a day and floss, I still felt like my teeth weren't getting clean enough.  My battle involves bleeding gums, which requires that much more cleaning power in between your teeth in order to get rid of the bacteria that's keeping them inflammed.  The Vitality brush does a pretty decent job of reaching deep into the surfaces and the spaces of your teeth to get them clean.  Licking my teeth, th

reviews.t: Only in a pinch...more like desperation.
reviews.x: My dentist took one look at my inflamed gums, and strongly suggested I start using an electric toothbrush.  I knew a cheapie like this wouldn't last, but I got it to tide me over until I got a proper electric brush.  Even so, this brush was so disagreeable that it induced me to shell out money sooner than I wanted to get a quality brush.  This comes packed with medium bristles.  I was wondering why it was so stiff, but then I went out and got a pack of soft bristles, which barely helped.  The pr

My family has several different Oral B electric toothbrush models. All give us that just polished feeling that one gets at the dentist! I prefer the models that have the 2 min auto timer, as it encourages spending that extra time to get all surfaces clean. The electric unit and timer are particularly useful for young children and older folks who may be suffering with limited hand dexterity due to arthritis and sore joints. I have given up manual toothbrushes forever and even take the Oral B when

reviews.t: broke down after 12 days but got another that's great
reviews.x: It worked great until yesterday when, after 12 days of use it wouldn't shut off, and now it won't turn on, it's kaput.  This is an update, I got a new one that works fine, we are very happy with it now.

reviews.t: metal from inner workings gets in toothpaste
reviews.x: I'm throwing this in the garbage (unfortunately the return window closed already) - must have been made in China, metal taste/gray metal bits exit holes in head and get mixed in with toothpaste. Get a pricey item like Sonicare - doesn't have this issue since parts are made with quality materials.  I'll probably be getting a Sonicare now.

reviews.t: Battery will not take a charge
reviews.x: I bought this product for my son 3 months ago.  It will no longer take a charge.  Can't recommend this product if it only lasts 3 months.

The brush died after 6 weeks of light use, alternating with a manual brush. In the meantime, the metal melted and caused noticeable taste and probably can be attributed for some metal accumulation on a tooth. This is not worth it even at this price.

reviews.t: Dead Battery | Replace | Another Dead Battery
reviews.x: Had one for 2 years, and it died of a dead battery.  Got another one and it lasted 1 year and now will not take a charge.

Never owned one of these electric jobs before. Could not believe how good it felt and how clean my teeth felt and looked. Hated brushing my teeth before and now I will look forward to the experience. Never wanted to spend the money before but now they are at an affordable price point. Why not have 2 and get all the different heads for a real professional clean?  Everyone should have one.

This electric toothbrush uses the same brush heads as Oral B's more expensive products, yet the price is very low.  It looks to be well-built, and it works just fine.  After trying it, I bought another one for my son.  He has difficulty brushing due to his braces, so I bought him the heads made specifically for that.

This is the fourth electric toothbrush I've owned in 7-8 years, and is by far my favorite.  I did love my Interplak brushes, which came recommended by my dentist as having the best cleaning action, but they were not durable (hence "brushes" and not "brush"). They say the key to getting an Interplak to last is to not use toothpaste, just dip the brush head into some Listerine. Sorry, but for me that wasn't a satisfying brushing experience.  After two Interplaks died, I moved on to Sonicare. That

I've used several prior versions of this toothbrush; this is an improved model. Small charging base uses little space on the vanity. Easy to grip with tapered, rubberized handle. Small brush head helps get into tight areas. Timer helps ensure proper amount of brushing. Brush refills are widely available. Great value.

reviews.t: Don't bother with the cheap one
reviews.x: I've been using some type of Oral B "spinny" toothbrush for years. My old one just died so I bought this one thinking that the price had come down a lot in the last 3-4 years. Apparently not. This one's a lot less expensive but you can tell. I *LOVE* the Oral B line of electric toothbrushes, but don't waste your time with the $20 version. But the $80+ ones - they really are that much better. This one spins so poorly; I know I'm not getting the cleaning I've enjoyed for years. I returned mine and

reviews.t: A Great Item For A Great Price
reviews.x: I've had this tooth brush for 2 weeks now and I'm very pleased with it. I'm a "hard-brusher" and I tend to bleed from my guns occasionally. This brush is very gentle on the gums, and I've yet to bleed using it. In fact, my teeth have never felt so clean before.  There are so many different brushes available out there, and they can get very expensive. I'm not sure what a $200 brush can do different than this one. It can't get much better than this. So, I highly recommend this to all!

I wanted a second brush for my downstairs bathroom so I could catch the kids before they went to school.  This is a great little brush for the money, it even has a two minute timer built in.  So far, so good.

Took a chance and bought 4 Oral B Vitality (the price was excellent). Have 2 teenage sons that don,t like to brush. At their last not so stellar dentist exam it was recommended electric toothbrushes. Received them a month ago and they really do work great. We all agree it gives that "just from the dentist clean feel". And the boys have even given me kudos on the choice. At first I felt the head was a little too small. But after a month of use we like the size because you have to concentrate on e

I used... Conair Interplak (9 months. Bought at Target)  I now use... Oral-B Vitality Precision Clean (2 months and counting. Bought on Amazon).  Comparison... 1) Batteries: Both are rechargeable (no need to fuss with buying and replacing batteries). Interplak recommends you run the batteries down every 6 months and then do a full recharge before use again. Oral-B encourages you to keep the toothbrush on the charger all the time, as they claim "there is no such thing as over-charging". Interplak

reviews.t: You get what you pay for.......
reviews.x: I bought this toothbrush about a week ago and ive already thrown it in the trash. The head on the brush hardly moves, it feels like its just vibrating more then anything else. I dont understand how others think this is a good brush.....

Even after a multi-day charging, this product chugs along with minimal power; if you bear down at all, it slows to a crawl. Then, when the two-minute timer goes off, it quits entirely, and refuses to restart. Useless.

This toothbrush does an excellent brushing job -- no need to buy a more expensive model.  I bought this one to replace a similar Oral B that lasted more than 8 years before the battery conked out.  Great product!

claims.text: Many reviewers consider it great value for the money and an affordable price point.
Several reviewers report the brush cleans well and leaves teeth feeling clean or polished.
Some reviewers report durability problems, including the brush dying or the battery failing to hold a charge.
Some reviewers report metal bits or a metallic taste mixing into their toothpaste.
Reviewers appreciate the 2-minute timer and find the brush easy to use.

qa.q: Does it fit replacement heads easily?
qa.answer: Reviews indicate replacement heads are easy to find and widely available [1][3], and one notes the brush uses the same heads as Oral B's more expensive products [2]. However, no review explicitly describes how easily the heads attach or fit onto the brush.

claims.text: Replacement heads are easy to find and cheap [1].
The brush uses the same brush heads as Oral B's more expensive products [2].

qa.q: How durable is the battery over time?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree on long-term battery durability: some report batteries dying after 1-2 years [2], while others say it holds the charge well so far [4]. One reviewer also wished battery life lasted longer than 5 days [1].

claims.text: Some report the battery died after 2 years, and a replacement lasted only 1 year before not taking a charge.
One reviewer says it holds the charge well so far.
One reviewer wished battery life was longer than 5 days.

qa.q: Is it comfortable to hold and use?
qa.answer: Reviews describe it as easy to grip with a tapered, rubberized handle [1] and light weight and easy to use [4].

claims.text: It is easy to grip with a tapered, rubberized handle.
It is light weight and easy to use.

qa.q: Is it safe for sensitive gums?
qa.answer: Not enough evidence in reviews to answer this.

qa.q: Is it good value for the price?
qa.answer: Most reviewers consider it good value for the price, calling it "great for the price" [1], "excellent value" [2], and "a great little brush for the money" [5]. However, one reviewer disagreed, saying "you get what you pay for" and throwing it away [6].

claims.text: Reviewers describe it as great for the price and excellent value.
One reviewer felt you get what you pay for and discarded it.
